name: graphify
description: Turn any codebase, with its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs, into a queryable knowledge graph. A /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI: local deterministic AST parsing, every edge explained, no vector store.
one_liner: A tool that reads an entire codebase — code, docs, database schemas, config files, PDFs — and turns it into a map you (or an AI) can search and ask questions about, with every connection explained.
buyer: An engineering manager who just inherited a legacy codebase (via a new hire, acquisition, or departed team) and needs to understand it fast.
business_use_cases: A new engineering hire gets a navigable architecture map on day one instead of spending weeks reading code to find how pieces connect.
A due-diligence consultant uses it to quickly map an acquisition target's codebase and flag architectural risk before a deal closes.
A legacy-modernization consultancy sells 'instant codebase map' as the first paid deliverable before quoting a bigger rewrite project.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a fixed-price 'codebase comprehension report' for companies onboarding new engineers or evaluating an acquisition.
Bundle it into ongoing legacy-system consulting retainers as the always-current reference map.

steal_this: Run it against a messy open-source or client repo this weekend, turn the output into a one-page 'how this codebase actually works' doc, and sell that doc as a fixed-price onboarding deliverable.
